condition: what a payment service provider may not do
state: borrow without the Central Bank's prior written approval; accept deposits; extend credit facilities; deal in any way in virtual currencies; issue debit payment instruments
note: Central Bank of Yemen, head office Aden: payment service provider instructions issued 13 September 2022; OCR text

condition: who bears a customer's losses when a payment or financial service fails, is breached or is defrauded
state: the payment service provider or system operator bears full responsibility, under its contracts and its responsibilities toward the services' beneficiaries, for faults, failures, breaches, leaks of information or mismanagement of accounts from clear and deliberate negligence, including the resulting losses
note: Central Bank of Yemen, head office Aden: payment service provider instructions issued 13 September 2022; OCR text

condition: who may set ceilings on payment instruments
state: the Central Bank may impose restrictions on payment service providers, including setting ceilings for payment instruments, to keep the financial system stable
note: Central Bank of Yemen, head office Aden: payment service provider instructions issued 13 September 2022; OCR text

condition: who may provide mobile e-money services
state: only a payment service provider licensed by the Central Bank to provide mobile e-money under these instructions, and a bank licensed by the Central Bank under circular 11 of 2014; a non-bank institution must first be licensed as a payment service provider
note: Central Bank of Yemen, head office Aden: instructions on mobile e-money services by non-bank financial institutions, dated 8 August 2023 (21 Muharram 1445); OCR text

condition: currencies in which mobile e-money may be held and transferred
state: the local currency (the Yemeni rial) only: issuers deal only in it, accounts open only in it, user-to-user transfers are in it only, and agents may not deal in any other currency; issuers may not offer currency exchange
note: Central Bank of Yemen, head office Aden: instructions on mobile e-money services by non-bank financial institutions, dated 8 August 2023 (21 Muharram 1445); OCR text

condition: limits on mobile e-money transactions and balances
state: individual accounts: 400,000 per transaction, 700,000 a day, 2,000,000 a month and 12,000,000 a year, counted cumulatively, and a balance of at most 2,000,000 rials; legal persons' accounts: limits set by the issuer with the Central Bank's prior written approval
note: Central Bank of Yemen, head office Aden: instructions on mobile e-money services by non-bank financial institutions, dated 8 August 2023 (21 Muharram 1445); OCR text

condition: what a buyer must provide to open a mobile e-money account
state: a national identity card with the national number (or a passport) and a service activation form with at least full name, ID or passport number, date of birth, address and mobile number; a legal person, its commercial register; a mobile number registered with a local telecom company
note: Central Bank of Yemen, head office Aden: instructions on mobile e-money services by non-bank financial institutions, dated 8 August 2023 (21 Muharram 1445); OCR text

condition: what identification a recipient without a mobile e-money account must show to collect a transfer
state: a national identity card with the national number, or a passport for foreigners, above 150,000 rials; at or below 150,000 rials, also an identity card without the national number, a family, military, social-security or voter card
note: Central Bank of Yemen, head office Aden: instructions on mobile e-money services by non-bank financial institutions, dated 8 August 2023 (21 Muharram 1445); OCR text; on line 322 the OCR reads '0 ريال' where the page image (page 07) shows 150,000

condition: how many mobile e-money accounts a customer may hold
state: no more than three accounts per customer in the service; each mobile number linked to one e-money account only, and each personal account to one mobile subscription with a network operator in the Republic
note: Central Bank of Yemen, head office Aden: instructions on mobile e-money services by non-bank financial institutions, dated 8 August 2023 (21 Muharram 1445); OCR text

condition: payments a buyer can make or receive through a wallet app
state: with mobile e-money: transfers to another e-money account, to and from a bank account, and to a person outside the service; paying utility bills (electricity, water, telephone); buying goods and services from merchants; receiving international remittances where these are received only through a commercial bank or remittance company; other services the Central Bank approves
note: Central Bank of Yemen, head office Aden: instructions on mobile e-money services by non-bank financial institutions, dated 8 August 2023 (21 Muharram 1445); OCR text

condition: whether a wallet balance may earn interest or incentives
state: no: the e-money issuer may grant no interest or incentive on a user's balance
note: Central Bank of Yemen, head office Aden: instructions on mobile e-money services by non-bank financial institutions, dated 8 August 2023 (21 Muharram 1445); OCR text

condition: whether a financial service provider may make exclusive arrangements with banks, telecom companies, agents or merchants
state: no: exclusivity is not allowed between the parties taking part in providing mobile e-money services
note: Central Bank of Yemen, head office Aden: instructions on mobile e-money services by non-bank financial institutions, dated 8 August 2023 (21 Muharram 1445); OCR text

condition: what a wallet agent may do and who may be one
state: agents may open mobile-linked accounts, buy and sell e-money and answer customers' questions and complaints; ordinary agents may not sub-contract other agents, deal in a currency other than the local one, or charge the customer more than the contract sets; an agent must be a Yemeni national with an identity card, or a legal person with a commercial register
note: Central Bank of Yemen, head office Aden: instructions on mobile e-money services by non-bank financial institutions, dated 8 August 2023 (21 Muharram 1445); OCR text

condition: how a financial service provider must handle customer complaints
state: complaints must be processed within a reasonable time, none later than 10 working days from notification, and the consumer told of the right to refer unresolved complaints to the Central Bank
note: Central Bank of Yemen, head office Aden: instructions on mobile e-money services by non-bank financial institutions, dated 8 August 2023 (21 Muharram 1445); OCR text

condition: what notice a wallet user gets of each transaction
state: an instant electronic notice (SMS or another channel) of each transaction made or received, showing the amount, the balance and the beneficiary's name
note: Central Bank of Yemen, head office Aden: instructions on mobile e-money services by non-bank financial institutions, dated 8 August 2023 (21 Muharram 1445); OCR text

condition: what a financial service provider must tell customers about its fees
state: a mobile e-money issuer must notify users in writing or electronically of changes to fees and charges at least two weeks before they take effect, and tell the Central Bank 14 days before; the Central Bank may publish the fees and commissions issuers collect
note: Central Bank of Yemen, head office Aden: instructions on mobile e-money services by non-bank financial institutions, dated 8 August 2023 (21 Muharram 1445); OCR text

condition: who is responsible for transactions made through a wallet account
state: the customer who requested the service with identity documents is responsible for all transactions through the mobile e-money account, not the person using the phone
note: Central Bank of Yemen, head office Aden: instructions on mobile e-money services by non-bank financial institutions, dated 8 August 2023 (21 Muharram 1445); OCR text

condition: who bears a customer's losses when a payment or financial service fails, is breached or is defrauded
state: the mobile e-money issuer bears full responsibility for any failure that harms the customer, whether by the settlement bank, the telecom company or the agent, within the service provided, and must cover their liability by contract
note: Central Bank of Yemen, head office Aden: instructions on mobile e-money services by non-bank financial institutions, dated 8 August 2023 (21 Muharram 1445); OCR text

condition: what electronic money must be issued against
state: mobile e-money is issued at a value equal to the funds received; the issuer may not hold the public's funds directly but must keep them in a pooled e-money (trust) account at a settlement bank, equal at all times to 100% of the outstanding e-money
note: Central Bank of Yemen, head office Aden: instructions on mobile e-money services by non-bank financial institutions, dated 8 August 2023 (21 Muharram 1445); OCR text; the page images show '100%' where the OCR reads '1100' (line 730, page 17) and 'لا يجوز' (may not) where the OCR reads 'Y -7 يجوز' (line 374, page 08)

condition: whether a wallet holder can redeem e-money for cash
state: yes: on the holder's request the issuer redeems e-money in cash at its equivalent value; issued e-money has no expiry date
note: Central Bank of Yemen, head office Aden: instructions on mobile e-money services by non-bank financial institutions, dated 8 August 2023 (21 Muharram 1445); OCR text

condition: how a financial service provider must handle customer complaints
state: answer every complaint with a decision within 10 working days of receiving it with all documents, extendable by 10 working days, and never beyond 30 working days; the consumer may take the complaint to the Central Bank within 14 days after the settlement period ends
note: Central Bank of Yemen, head office Aden: regulatory instructions on financial consumer protection, issued 20 August 2023 (4 Safar 1445); OCR text

condition: what a financial service provider must tell customers about its fees
state: charge no fee not disclosed in advance; publish interest rates, fees and other charges at least every three months in Arabic and English in at least one widely read newspaper; show products, services and fees on its website and prominently at its premises; tell the Central Bank 5 working days before publishing; notify the consumer in writing, including electronically, before changing fees or interest
note: Central Bank of Yemen, head office Aden: regulatory instructions on financial consumer protection, issued 20 August 2023 (4 Safar 1445); OCR text; the page image (page 24) reads 'كل ثلاثة أشهر على الأقل' where the OCR has 'كل BNE أشهر' (line 995)

condition: whether a financial service provider may make exclusive arrangements with banks, telecom companies, agents or merchants
state: no: a financial service provider may not take part in exclusive arrangements with agents and merchants
note: Central Bank of Yemen, head office Aden: regulatory instructions on financial consumer protection, issued 20 August 2023 (4 Safar 1445); OCR text

condition: whether a payment provider's system must work with other providers' systems
state: a financial service provider must use interoperable systems
note: Central Bank of Yemen, head office Aden: regulatory instructions on financial consumer protection, issued 20 August 2023 (4 Safar 1445); OCR text

condition: whether a payment provider's system must work with other providers' systems
state: a mobile e-money system must be ready and able to interoperate once an interoperability platform is available, at least supporting ISO 20022 or other messages the Central Bank adopts
note: Central Bank of Yemen, head office Aden: instructions on mobile e-money services by non-bank financial institutions, dated 8 August 2023 (21 Muharram 1445); OCR text; '15020022' in the OCR is ISO20022 on the page image (page 06)

condition: who bears a customer's losses when a payment or financial service fails, is breached or is defrauded
state: the financial service provider bears consumers' losses from fraud, embezzlement or misuse of the financial assets it or its agent holds and manages, and must return the money lost, unless the consumer's negligence or fraudulent conduct is proved to have caused it
note: Central Bank of Yemen, head office Aden: regulatory instructions on financial consumer protection, issued 20 August 2023 (4 Safar 1445); OCR text

condition: whether a customer may end a financial service or move it to another provider
state: yes: consumers are free to deal with any financial service provider; providers may not restrict ending agreements or switching to another provider, and must act on the consumer's request within 30 days of notice
note: Central Bank of Yemen, head office Aden: regulatory instructions on financial consumer protection, issued 20 August 2023 (4 Safar 1445); OCR text

condition: whether a buyer can open a bank or wallet account remotely, without visiting the provider
state: yes, for natural persons only: banks and providers licensed for mobile e-money may, with the Central Bank's prior written approval, onboard customers remotely by electronic know-your-customer with biometric identity checks; legal persons follow the regular procedure; exchange companies are not covered; for current and savings accounts the customer must also show an existing account at another licensed institution
place: Central Bank of Yemen (head office Aden)'s area
note: Central Bank of Yemen, head office Aden: instructions regulating electronic know-your-customer procedures, dated 25 Rabi al-Akhir 1445 / 9 November 2023 (page image 16; the OCR of lines 665-666 garbles both dates); the scope names institutions, not an area; OCR text

condition: whether electronic records and signatures have the legal effect of written ones
state: yes, for records and signatures made in electronic customer onboarding or in providing financial or banking services, provided the requirements of the electronic payments and banking transactions law (no. 40 of 2006) and these instructions are met
place: Central Bank of Yemen (head office Aden)'s area
note: Central Bank of Yemen, head office Aden: instructions regulating electronic know-your-customer procedures, dated 25 Rabi al-Akhir 1445 / 9 November 2023 (page image 16); the scope names institutions, not an area; OCR text

condition: which e-wallets and e-payment services banks and exchange companies may deal with
state: none that the Central Bank has not licensed: direct and indirect dealing is prohibited with the Cash, Al-Dawli Money, Jawali, Floosak, Saba Cash, Mobile Money, Yemen Wallet, E-Rial, Rial Mobile, Jaib, WeCash and Al-Mutakamila wallets, named as unlicensed, and with any other unlicensed e-wallet or service
note: Central Bank of Yemen, head office Aden, banking supervision sector: circular CBY/L/282/2024 to all banks and exchange companies; the page image shows 'Date:26/06/2024' and the heading '... العاملة في الجمهورية', which the OCR omits or truncates (lines 10-13); OCR text

condition: currencies in which mobile e-money may be held and transferred
state: the local currency and the major foreign currencies (US dollar, Saudi riyal, UAE dirham): accounts may be opened and transfers made in them; issuers may not convert local currency into any foreign currency
place: Central Bank of Yemen (head office Aden)'s area
note: Central Bank of Yemen, head office Aden: Governor's decision no. 4 of 2025 amending the mobile e-money instructions of 8/9 August 2023 (item 050), in force from its issue on 9 July 2025 (14 Muharram 1447); the decision names no area of its own; OCR text

state: individual accounts in local currency: 1,000,000 rials per transaction, 2,000,000 a day, 5,000,000 a month, 50,000,000 a year, and a balance of at most 8,000,000 rials; in the major foreign currencies: 400, 500, 1,000 and 10,000 US dollars or equivalent, and a balance of at most 1,500 dollars; legal persons: set by the issuer with the Central Bank's prior written approval
place: Central Bank of Yemen (head office Aden)'s area
note: Central Bank of Yemen, head office Aden: Governor's decision no. 4 of 2025 amending the mobile e-money instructions of 8/9 August 2023 (item 050), in force from its issue on 9 July 2025 (14 Muharram 1447); the decision names no area of its own; OCR text; the figures are read from page image 2, the OCR of the table and of the balance cap being garbled (lines 74-94)

condition: what electronic money must be issued against
state: issued against receipt of funds of the same value in the local currency or in the major foreign currencies (US dollar, Saudi riyal, UAE dirham)
place: Central Bank of Yemen (head office Aden)'s area
note: Central Bank of Yemen, head office Aden: Governor's decision no. 4 of 2025 amending the mobile e-money instructions of 8/9 August 2023 (item 050), in force from its issue on 9 July 2025 (14 Muharram 1447); the decision names no area of its own; OCR text

condition: what a bank or exchange company must check before carrying out a customer's transaction
state: screen the customer and its beneficial owners against the UN Security Council, OFAC, EU, UK Treasury and local sanctions lists before and during any banking or commercial transaction, with specialised screening systems; refuse or stop dealings with any listed customer and report matches to the Financial Information Unit
note: Central Bank of Yemen, head office Aden, banking supervision sector: periodic circular no. 4 of 2025 to all banks and exchange companies operating in the Republic, dated 02/11/2025 (lines 11, 111); OCR text

condition: whether a financial service provider may deal in virtual assets or use them for payments
state: no: banks, exchange companies and payment service and e-wallet providers and operators in the Yemeni banking sector may not, directly or indirectly, for themselves, their customers or others, buy, sell, trade, exchange, transfer, move, hold or manage virtual assets, use virtual assets as a means of payment, transfer, settlement or meeting obligations through their products or services, or carry out, receive or facilitate transfers or payments made to buy, sell, trade or transfer virtual assets
place: Central Bank of Yemen (head office Aden)'s area
